author: Clare Gehlich
title: Trinity Episcopal head of school to retire as criminal investigation involving high school students continues - NewsBreak
text:
By Clare Gehlich ,
10 hours ago
RICHMOND, Va. (WRIC) — As Trinity Episcopal School faces scrutiny over a criminal investigation involving several high school students , the head of school announced plans Wednesday to retire after more than a decade.
In an email sent to the school community on Wednesday, Oct. 14, Rob Short, Trinity's head of school, announced his retirement following his fourth term. He notified the Board of Trustees in June 2026 that the 2026-27 school year would be his last.
"I am deeply grateful for the opportunity to serve as head of school and for the experiences and relationships that have made my time here filled with meaning, purpose and lifelong friends," Short said in his email. "We have accomplished so much during my time at Trinity, and we’ve done it all together, which is so very Trinity."
Cynthia Coleman, chair of the Board of Trustees, also expressed her appreciation for Short in a message sent to the Trinity community Wednesday.
"In June, Rob shared with the board his desire to retire at the end of the 2026-27 school year," Coleman said.
In more than five decades, Coleman said Trinity has had only four heads of school, adding that the stability is one of the school's greatest strengths and a lasting part of Short's legacy.
The Board of Trustees has formed a search committee comprising trustees, faculty, advisory board members and alumni. The committee will be co-chaired by Chris Ellis, an alumna and former board chair, and Jana McQuaid, the current board vice chair.
"The goal of the board and the search committee is to ensure a seamless transition," Coleman said. "We want Trinity Episcopal School to find the head of school for the Trinity of today and the school we will build for tomorrow."
The Board of Trustees has engaged IndySchool Consultancy, a firm that specializes in leadership searches for independent schools, according to Coleman. Two of their representatives will work with Trinity's search committee throughout the process. They will visit campus early next week to listen to faculty, staff, students, parents, alumni and trustees.
School leadership will launch a website to keep the community informed throughout the search.
Short's retirement announcement comes as Trinity has been the center of controversy after a criminal investigation launched on Thursday, Sept. 24, into allegations of sexual misconduct, nonconsensual photo sharing and other concerning behaviors involving high school students.
MORE: Trinity Episcopal students accused of sexual misconduct, sharing photos of others without consent In an email Trinity Episcopal leadership sent out to students and families on Monday, Sept. 28, school officials said that “a group of Trinity boys were required to remain off-campus while the school worked to understand the scope of the alleged violations of school policies."
The school briefly shifted to a fully asynchronous and virtual learning day on Wednesday, Sept. 23, and opened late on Thursday, Sept. 24.
Trinity introduced a new "away for the day" cell phone policy, requiring students to keep phones stored in their backpacks all day.
